regions.region: page 1 title, author block, abstract, and graphical abstract
regions.finding: Verified the source title and aggregate Ni/photoredox allenylation claim. The graphical abstract is a generic current reaction class and is linked to Scheme 1c rather than treated as an experiment-specific run.
The organometallic nucleophilic approach and Wang reductive alkyl-iodide approach are cited background. They are represented as literature examples, not current-paper experiments.
The 1a/2a/(TMS)3SiH model reaction begins here and continues in Table 1 on page 2; it is represented once as Table 1 entry 1 with cross-page evidence.

unresolved: Generic graphical-abstract and Scheme 1 structures contain R groups and do not define unique molecules.
The paper links online SI, but workspace SI association remains unestablished.

regions.finding: Classified panel a and panel b as prior strategies and panel c as the current generic strategy. No table-row yield was assigned to these generic diagrams.

regions.region: page 2 center/left Table 1 header, entries 1-15, catalyst/ligand structures, and footnotes
regions.finding: Recorded all 15 optimization rows independently, including omitted catalyst/ligand/PC/light/silane/base controls, ligand/PC replacements, 405 nm DPA footnote, leaving-group variants, 19F-NMR product yields, and starting-electrophile recoveries.
Mapped prose to the same 15 rows. Entry 13 retains zero desired-product yield and the selectively formed allenic reduction product as distinct outcomes.

Linked functional-group scope prose to Table 2 rows. The cyclohexyl I/Br/Cl comparison is represented as two low-yield control rows plus the existing product-15 bromide row, which retains both 68% isolated and 71% NMR yields. Tertiary bromide failures remain separate tests.

unresolved: Table 1 omits temperature, atmosphere, workup, purification, isolated masses, and detection limits.
Compact scope structures remain source-labeled where safe SMILES encoding was uncertain.

regions.region: page 3 upper Table 2 reaction header and product grid 3-35
regions.finding: Recorded all 33 displayed product rows independently with the shared catalyst/PC/base/silane/acetone/light conditions, isolated yields, and row-specific scale, ligand/loading, time, equimolar, and catalyst-recharge footnotes.

Retained six distinct tests: cyclohexyl iodide and chloride with 1%/5% NMR yields, plus source-depicted alkynyl-chain bromide, aminoalkyl bromide hydrobromide, tert-butyl bromide, and 1-bromoadamantane qualitative failures. The amino substrate receives the 2.5-equiv-base footnote.

Mapped propargyl-carbonate scope prose to rows 21-35. Product 34 retains 23% yield versus 70% conversion; product 35 retains 10% yield versus full conversion. Degradation is a note, not a fabricated product yield.

regions.region: page 3 lower-right Ni(0) and CV mechanistic experiments
regions.finding: Recorded the Ni(COD)2/L1 probe giving allene 16 in 25% and one CV series with the printed -1.44/-1.78 V waves and the 5/10-equiv carbonate perturbations. These are distinct from the preparative scope row and proposed mechanism.

unresolved: Table 2 does not report temperature, atmosphere, workup, purification, or isolated masses.
The 48 h row reports catalyst recharge at 24 h but not a separate post-addition duration; no arithmetic stage time was invented.
CV setup details are only referred to unassociated SI.

regions.finding: Recorded one model-reaction TEMPO control: product formation was completely suppressed and no TEMPO adduct was observed. TEMPO dose and analytical limits remain missing.
Recorded the cyclopropylmethyl-bromide standard-condition experiment separately, giving ring-opened allene 36 as the sole coupling product in 22% reported yield.

regions.region: page 4 mechanistic discussion and lower Scheme 2
regions.finding: Classified A-F and the Ni/silyl-radical cycle as a proposed mechanism, not preparations. Ni(0) and bromine-radical alternatives remain unresolved. GC-MS detection of (TMS)3Si-OMe is linked both to the standard model run and the mechanism as coproduct evidence.
The paper advertises online experimental procedures/characterization, but this does not establish a workspace SI association and no SI-only facts were imported.

unresolved: TEMPO dose and equation-1 yield basis/operational details are absent from the main text.
Mechanistic intermediates and competing pathways are proposed, not independently observed.

regions.region: page 5 left column author information, contributions, notes, acknowledgments, and references 1-7
regions.finding: Administrative material and bibliography only; cited external papers were not expanded into experiments of this article.

Most content is prior literature. Footnote 15's ineffective TMS3SiNH-(adamantan-1-yl) XAT agent is retained as a qualitative unresolved failure, and footnote 16's stoichiometric 2a/L1/Ni(COD)2 homocoupling is retained as a separate mechanistic control.

unresolved: Footnote 15 omits the exact alkyl chloride and full reaction recipe.
Footnote 16 omits solvent, time, temperature, product identity, yield, and analytical method.
Other references are external prior work and were not imported.

regions.region: page 6 references 19-22 and footnote 20 alternative pathway
regions.finding: The page is bibliography plus mechanistic commentary. Footnote 20's possible bromine-radical route is linked as unresolved context to the existing Scheme 2 mechanism; no new reaction experiment occurs.
The lower and right portions of the rendered original page are blank and contain no reaction arrow, table, condition, outcome, or footnote reagent.

unresolved: The bromine-radical alternative cannot be ruled out by the authors.
No current-paper preparative experiment occurs on this page.
External references were not expanded into current-paper records.
